hypothesis: H8 reverse split: bead on the COARSE levels (i=4,5,6) + hexagon on the FINE levels reads more clearly than bead everywhere, and as a real uniform branch is cheaper
why: Perf YES, legibility NO. Measured by RMS luminance distance between arms (controller-off, seed-pinned, full res): the 3 COARSE levels carry 93.6% (kiku) / 91.7% (ume) of the entire bead effect, the 3 FINE levels only 6.0% / 6.8% - so H3 lost because it bought 6% of the effect. But rev-split does not read CLEARER than all-bead, it reads ~93% IDENTICALLY to it, and all-bead is marginally more coherent because every scale agrees on one motif while rev-split shows straight fine filigree inside curved coarse cells. The predicted risk landed: the coarse levels ARE the structural skeleton, so rev-split destroys the straight-line hexagonal frame exactly as all-bead does. REUSABLE MECHANISM: the levels that carry the motif and the levels that carry the skeleton are the SAME levels - no recursion-depth split can keep the familiar frame AND show the bead. Lit coverage shows the size mechanism directly: fwd-split raises lit>20 most (5.63->6.68pt) but bright>50 least (0.57->0.85) = diffuse speckle; rev-split barely moves lit (5.63->5.77) but triples bright (0.57->1.49) = fewer, larger, stronger marks. Perf as a REAL BRANCH (not mix, which evaluates both operands): all-hex 0.390, all-bead 0.483, fwd-split 0.378, rev-split 0.382 ms/frame offscreen 2048^2 - rev-split is 21% cheaper than all-bead and indistinguishable from all-hex, i.e. 93% of the look for none of the cost. Settled split point i=4,5,6 (recovery 62.4/84.4/93.4% for 1/2/3 coarse levels; ms/frame flat across all three).
next: Adopt rev-split (i=4,5,6) as the DEFAULT bead configuration on cost grounds alone - it is visually equivalent to all-bead and 21% cheaper. Do not expect it to fix legibility.
